The SQL test harness exists (`supabase/tests/helpers.sql` with the `app_test` builders, session switchers and assertions; `scripts/db/test.sh` extended) and three structural tests — `01_tenancy` (cross-org isolation, anon denial, no 42P17), `08_rerunnable` (re-apply inside a transaction, identical object counts, every function definer + search_path) and `09_grants` (the grant matrix by `has_function_privilege`/`has_column_privilege`) — pass in the standing local sequence.

## Goal

Read `9999_init.sql` end to end first: the exact function signatures in (5a)/(5c) are what section (9) grants, and the column names fixed in 1.2 are what the policies reference.
- Founder decisions that apply here: decision 7 — "only `suspended` blocks writes; `past_due` = banner only" (every write policy uses `app.org_writable(org_id)`, which 1.3a defined as `status in ('trial','active','past_due')`); decision 5 — share links are "available to `sermons.link` OR `sermons.upload` holders" (`sermon_share_links` select policy); decision 4 — the permission mapping in DESIGN §5 ships as the default (directory admin = `users.create` or `org.settings`; custom groups = `announcements.create` or `org.settings`; surveys = `announcements.create/edit/delete`; calendar CRUD = `org.settings`; billing status and audit = `org.settings`); decision 10 — "Supabase FREE plan … 50 MB per-file upload cap (bucket `file_size_limit` for `sermon-media` must be ≤ 50 MiB while on Free; keep the value in one place and document raising it on Pro)" (orchestrator decision 4: one documented constant at the top of the storage section; bucket rows are upserted, so a later `9998_*` paste can raise it to 2 GiB on Pro without editing the frozen file).
- `9999_init.sql` is NOT frozen (empty HANDOFF ledger): earlier sections may be edited when a policy needs it — record each edit under HANDOFF "Deviations from plan".

## Build
Work inside `9999_init.sql` sections (8)–(11), `supabase/tests/00_shim.sql` (one local-only tweak), `supabase/tests/helpers.sql`, `supabase/tests/rls/{01_tenancy,08_rerunnable,09_grants}.sql`, `scripts/db/test.sh`, plus the docs/handoff edits in Finish.

**Mandatory mid-step checkpoint (sizing):** this step holds two large bodies of work — the policy catalogue (sections 8–11) and the harness. As soon as sections (8)–(11) apply twice and `bash scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh` passes (the psql counts in Verify are the only checks at that point; `test.sh` still reports no behavioural tests), commit and push `feat(db): RLS policy catalogue, grants and storage buckets (9999 sections 8–11)` BEFORE starting `helpers.sql`. If the session ends there, the repo is consistent and the next session resumes at item 6 of this list. The step's final commit uses the commit message in Finish.

1. **Section (8) RLS baseline** — copy the DESIGN §4.4 block: the `do $$` loop that runs `alter table public.%I enable row level security` for every table in `pg_tables where schemaname = 'public'` (NO `force`: the owner-bypass scheme requires it). Then make table privileges explicit instead of relying on Supabase's default privileges (the local shim has none): `grant select, insert, update, delete on all tables in schema public to authenticated; grant all on all tables in schema public to service_role; revoke all on all tables in schema public from anon; revoke all on all tables in schema private from anon, authenticated, service_role;` (add `revoke usage on schema private` here if section (1) lacks it). This positive grant block is an addition to DESIGN §4.4, which relies on Supabase's default privileges for `authenticated`/`service_role` (its section (1) only revokes the `anon` default): it is required by the local shim and harmless on Supabase — record it under HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" and note there that step 1.5 must put it in docs/MIGRATIONS.md as the rule "every new table created by a `9998_*` migration needs its own grant line". Then the column-level block verbatim from DESIGN §4.4: `revoke all on public.persons, public.households from authenticated;` followed by `grant select (id, org_id, household_id, user_id, first_name, last_name, preferred_name, sex, household_role, congregation_status, directory_listed, photo_path, email, mobile_phone, work_phone, deceased_on, marital_status, birthdate_visibility, created_at, updated_at) on public.persons to authenticated;` and `grant select (id, org_id, name, address_line1, address_line2, city, region, postal_code, country, home_phone, photo_path, sort_key, created_at, updated_at) on public.households to authenticated;` (no `birthdate`, `member_since`, `youth_override`, `anniversary`, privacy flags, `privacy_confirmed_*`, `created_via`). Reconcile both column lists against the real `create table` statements in section (3) before pasting: the rule is DESIGN's intent (everything except the columns just listed), the names are section (3)'s — step 1.2 fixed the real column names (for example the phone columns) and a verbatim copy fails the paste if any differ. Then the RPC-only `revoke insert, update, delete … from authenticated` verbatim from DESIGN (persons, households, both leader-notes tables, org_memberships, org_membership_permissions, invitations, join_codes, join_requests, sermon_share_links, billing_customers, billing_subscriptions, stripe_events, notifications, notification_deliveries, audit_log, storage_deletions, account_deletion_requests, super_admins). Re-issue `grant select on public.directory_households, public.directory_persons, public.org_directory_info to authenticated;` (views are owned by the migration owner, so they read the base tables with owner privileges; the functions they call — `app.household_view_level`, `app.is_adult`, `app.member_org_ids`, `app.fellowship_visible_org_ids` — are executed with the CALLER's privileges, which is why section (9) grants them to `authenticated`).
2. **Section (8) policy catalogue** — one `drop policy if exists <name> on <table>;` immediately before each `create policy`, names `ca_<table>_<op>_<who>`, every write policy also requires `app.org_writable(org_id)`, and viewer facts always in the InitPlan form `org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids()))` / `org_id = any((select app.perm_org_ids('<perm>')))` (never a correlated call per row). `service_role` gets no policies (BYPASSRLS). Implement DESIGN §6's table:
   - `organizations`: select `ca_orgs_select_fellowship` (verbatim from DESIGN: member or `app.fellowship_visible_org_ids()`); insert/update `ca_organizations_insert_super` / `ca_organizations_update_super` (`app.is_super_admin()`); no delete policy (`cancelled` + purge).
   - `organization_settings`: select member (`ca_organization_settings_select_member`); update `ca_organization_settings_update_org_settings` = `org.settings` ∧ writable; no insert/delete policy (the `on_org_created` trigger inserts as definer).
   - `fellowships` / `fellowship_memberships`: select when the caller is a member of a linked org (`exists (select 1 from public.fellowship_memberships fm where fm.fellowship_id = <id> and fm.org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids())))`) or super admin; insert/update/delete super only.
   - `profiles`: `ca_profiles_select_org_admin` verbatim from DESIGN (own row, or a `users.create`/`users.delete`/`users.edit_permissions` holder of a shared org); insert/update own row (`user_id = auth.uid()`); no delete.
   - `super_admins`: select super only; no writes (bootstrap INSERT runs as `postgres`).
   - `org_memberships`, `org_membership_permissions`: select own row (`user_id = auth.uid()`, via the membership for the permissions table) or any `users.*` holder of the org; no write policies (RPC-only; the revoke above already removes the privilege — the absence of policies is the second lock).
   - `invitations`, `join_codes`: select `users.create`; `join_requests`: select `users.create` or own (`user_id = auth.uid()`); no write policies.
   - `households` / `persons`: `ca_households_select_visible` / `ca_persons_select_visible` = `exists (select 1 from public.directory_households d where d.id = households.id)` (DESIGN: "base table only through the view's rule"); no write policies. `household_leader_notes` / `person_leader_notes`: select `org_id = any((select app.directory_admin_org_ids()))`; no write policies.
   - `audience_groups`: select member; insert/update/delete `announcements.create` or `org.settings` ∧ writable, and delete additionally `kind = 'custom'` (system rows are never deleted). `audience_group_members`: select, insert, delete for the same manager pair only; no update policy.
   - `calendars`: select member ∧ `app.user_in_group(view_audience_group_id)`; insert/update/delete `org.settings` ∧ writable.
   - `events`: select member ∧ calendar visible (`exists (select 1 from public.calendars c where c.id = events.calendar_id)` — the calendar policy applies inside the subquery) ∧ (`status = 'approved'` ∨ `submitted_by = auth.uid()` ∨ `announcements.edit`); insert member ∧ writable ∧ (`organization_settings.members_can_submit_events` ∨ `announcements.create`) ∧ `app.user_in_group(<calendar's submit_audience_group_id>)` (DESIGN §6 lists only `members_can_submit_events`; the `∨ announcements.create` branch is this step's reading so managers are never blocked by the member toggle — 1.4c tests it; record it under Deviations) ∧ `submitted_by = auth.uid()` (the 1.3a trigger forces `pending`/`push = false` for non-creators); update `using` own-while-pending or `announcements.edit`, `with check` the same plus `status = 'pending'` unless `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete` or own pending.
   - `sermons`: `ca_sermons_select_members` and `ca_sermons_insert_by_kind` verbatim from DESIGN §4.4; `ca_sermons_update_by_kind` with the same media-kind split in both `using` and `with check`; `ca_sermons_delete_sermons_delete` = `sermons.delete` ∧ writable.
   - `sermon_share_links`: select `sermons.link` or `sermons.upload`; no write policies (RPC-only).
   - `announcements`: select member ∧ `publish_at <= now()` ∧ (`expires_at is null or expires_at > now()`) ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or any of `announcements.create/edit/delete`; insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit`; delete `announcements.delete` — each ∧ writable.
   - `bulletins`: select member ∧ `publish_at <= now()`, or `bulletins.upload`; insert/update/delete `bulletins.upload` ∧ writable. `documents`: select member ∧ published ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or `documents.upload`; writes `documents.upload` ∧ writable.
   - `surveys`, `survey_questions`: select member ∧ `status = 'open'` ∧ inside `[opens_at, closes_at]` (nulls open-ended) ∧ `app.user_in_group(audience_group_id)`, or any of `announcements.create/edit/delete` (DESIGN §6 says `announcements.create` only; the three-key form follows the PLAN §4 / DESIGN §5 survey mapping `announcements.create/edit/delete` — record it under Deviations) (questions via `exists` on the parent survey); insert `announcements.create`; update `announcements.edit` (the 1.3a `freeze_survey_shape` trigger guards the shape); delete `announcements.delete`.
   - `survey_responses`: select own (`person_id = app.my_person_id(org_id)` or `household_id = any((select app.my_household_ids()))`) or the three announcement permissions; insert member ∧ writable ∧ survey open/in window/in audience (the `stamp_response_scope` trigger overwrites the scope columns); update own ∧ survey open ∧ `allow_edit` (per_household → any adult of the household through `my_household_ids`); no delete. `survey_answers`: select/insert/update through `exists` on the visible/own response with the same conditions; no delete.
   - `push_devices`, `notification_preferences`: one `for all` policy each, `using`/`with check` `user_id = auth.uid()` (preferences additionally `org_id = any((select app.member_org_ids()))` in `with check`).
   - `notifications`: select for any `announcements.*` holder; no write policies. `notification_deliveries`, `stripe_events`, `storage_deletions`: select super admin only. `billing_customers`, `billing_subscriptions`: select `org.settings` or super. `audit_log`: select `org.settings` or super; no writes (trigger-fed as definer). `account_deletion_requests`: select own.
   Every public table ends up with at least one select policy.
3. **Section (9) grants** — copy the DESIGN §4.4 block verbatim: `revoke execute on all functions in schema public from public, anon, authenticated; revoke execute on all functions in schema app from public, anon, authenticated;` then the three `grant execute` statements: the `app.*` helper list to `authenticated` (add `app.can_read_object(text, text)` and `app.can_write_object(text, text)` because the storage policies call them as the querying role; add `app.person_in_group(uuid, uuid)` only if a policy references it directly), the 17 client RPCs to `authenticated` with DESIGN's exact signatures (`my_context`, `set_membership_permissions`, `set_membership_status`, `remove_membership`, `create_invitation`, `revoke_invitation`, `accept_invitation`, `save_household`, `save_person`, `delete_person`, `set_household_privacy`, `save_leader_notes`, `set_congregation_status`, `create_share_link`, `revoke_share_link`, `submit_survey_response`, `request_account_deletion`), and the 7 `srv_*` RPCs to `service_role` only (`srv_resolve_share_link`, `srv_audience_user_ids`, `srv_enqueue_due_notifications`, `srv_claim_notifications`, `srv_attach_user`, `srv_process_account_deletions`, `srv_housekeeping`). If a 1.3b signature differs from DESIGN's, the grant must match the real function (grants on a non-existent signature fail the paste) and the difference goes to HANDOFF. `anon` receives nothing. Trigger functions, `app.require_*`, `app.rate_limit_*`, `app.person_in_kind` and every `srv_*` stay unreachable for `authenticated`.
4. **Section (10) storage** — start with the single constant: a `do $$ declare c_sermon_media_limit bigint := 52428800; -- 50 MiB: Supabase FREE plan cap (founder decision 10). To raise it on Pro: raise the project's global upload limit in the dashboard, then ship a new migration (supabase/migrations/9995_storage_limit.sql) that repeats ONLY this bucket upsert for sermon-media with 2147483648 (2 GiB) — never edit this file once it is in the HANDOFF ledger. Keep NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB (docs/ENV.md) in sync. begin … end $$;` block that executes the `insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types) values … on conflict (id) do update set public = excluded.public, file_size_limit = excluded.file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types = excluded.allowed_mime_types` statement from DESIGN §4.4 with these rows: `sermon-media` (`c_sermon_media_limit`, MIME `audio/mpeg, audio/mp4, audio/aac, audio/ogg, audio/wav, audio/x-m4a, video/mp4, video/quicktime, video/webm`), `bulletins` (26214400; `application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png`), `documents` (52428800; the DESIGN allow-list: pdf, jpeg, png, text/plain, msword, docx, xls, xlsx), `directory-photos` (10485760; jpeg, png, webp), `org-assets` (5242880; jpeg, png, webp — no SVG). All `public = false`. Then the two policies: `drop policy if exists ca_storage_select on storage.objects; create policy ca_storage_select on storage.objects for select to authenticated using (app.can_read_object(bucket_id, name));` and `ca_storage_insert … for insert to authenticated with check (app.can_write_object(bucket_id, name));` — NO update/delete policies for `authenticated` (DESIGN §6: deletions only via `storage_deletions` + service role). Do not `enable row level security` on `storage.objects` in the migration (Supabase already has it; `postgres` does not own the table) — the shim does it locally (item 6).
5. **Section (11) bootstrap** — the commented block from DESIGN §4.4 with a placeholder instead of any real address: `-- insert into public.super_admins (user_id) select id from auth.users where email = '<FOUNDER_EMAIL>' on conflict do nothing;` with comment lines: paste AFTER signing up once on the deployed site; replace `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`; record the date in the HANDOFF ledger. No real email in the file.
6. **`supabase/tests/00_shim.sql`** (local-only): add, idempotently, three tweaks that mirror Supabase: `alter role service_role bypassrls;` (`login_service()` relies on it), `alter table storage.objects enable row level security;` (guarded via `pg_class.relrowsecurity`), and `grant select, insert, update, delete on storage.objects, storage.buckets to authenticated, service_role;` (Supabase grants these table privileges; G2's shim granted only `select`, and without `insert`/`update`/`delete` the storage tests in 1.4c would fail with 42501 before any policy is exercised — the `ca_storage_*` policies and the ABSENCE of update/delete policies are what filter). Make the tweaks reach existing databases: change `scripts/db/local-up.sh` so that it always applies `supabase/tests/00_shim.sql` (the shim is fully idempotent) instead of skipping it when `auth.uid()` already exists — a one-line change; keep the fast path for an already-running cluster. Record the change in HANDOFF (1.2 documented the skip). If you prefer not to touch `local-up.sh`, the fallback is `psql "$(cat .local-pg/PG_SUPER_URL)" -c "drop database churchapp"` then `bash scripts/db/local-up.sh` — but then every other machine (the founder's agents at 1.4b/1.4c/1.5) needs the same manual step, so prefer the script change. CI starts fresh either way.
7. **`supabase/tests/helpers.sql`** — re-runnable (`create schema if not exists app_test`, `create or replace function`), header "test helpers — apply before `tests/rls/*.sql`; local and hosted SQL editor; never part of a migration". `grant usage on schema app_test to anon, authenticated, service_role` and `grant execute on all functions in schema app_test to anon, authenticated, service_role` at the end. Two families:
   - Fixture builders, `security definer set search_path = ''` (they bypass RLS whatever role the test currently runs as — but NOT the 1.3a trigger guards, see the identity rule below): `app_test.make_user(email text) returns uuid` (insert into `auth.users`; the 1.3a trigger creates the profile), `app_test.make_org(slug text) returns uuid` (insert `organizations` with `name = slug`, `status = 'trial'`, `trial_ends_at = now() + interval '30 days'`; the trigger creates settings, 6 groups, 4 calendars), `app_test.make_member(org uuid, uid uuid, perms public.permission_key[] default '{}', status public.membership_status default 'active') returns uuid` (membership in the given status + permission rows; 1.4c needs `disabled` memberships and 1.5's seed `pending`/`disabled` ones without hand-editing `org_memberships`, which would fire the last-manager trigger (1.3a's name)), `app_test.make_fellowship(slug text, orgs uuid[]) returns uuid`, `app_test.make_household(org uuid, name text, created_via text default 'self') returns uuid`, `app_test.make_person(org uuid, hh uuid, first_name text, opts jsonb default '{}') returns uuid` (opts keys = `persons` column names, applied with `jsonb_populate_record`-style mapping), `app_test.set_setting(org uuid, col text, val text)` (dynamic `update organization_settings`), `app_test.sha256_token(token text) returns bytea` (the 1.3b convention `sha256(convert_to(token, 'UTF8'))`), `app_test.make_super(email text default 'super@example.test') returns uuid` (`make_user` + a `super_admins` row; returns the existing id when the email exists).
   - **Identity rule for fixtures** (1.4b, 1.4c and 1.5 rely on it): builders and direct content inserts are executed while logged out (`app_test.logout()` — role `churchapp_owner`, `auth.uid()` null). Bypassing RLS is not enough: 1.3a's guards (`guard_persons_columns`, `guard_household_privacy_columns`, `force_event_pending`, `stamp_response_scope`, `assert_same_org`, the last-manager trigger (1.3a's name)) fire regardless of role and read `auth.uid()`. Read those functions FIRST. If every guard treats `auth.uid() is null` as a trusted owner/service context, nothing more to do. Otherwise do not weaken the guards — make every builder save `current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true)`, `perform set_config('request.jwt.claims', <claims of a per-run super admin created lazily by app_test.make_super()>, true)` for the duration of the call, and restore the previous value on exit (also on exception). Either way, state the convention in the `helpers.sql` header comment and in HANDOFF, and prove it in 01_tenancy: `make_person(... congregation_status => 'member')` stores `member`, and an `events` row inserted with `status = 'approved'` by the harness stays `approved`.
   - Session and assertion helpers, `security invoker` so RLS and grants apply to the current role: `app_test.login(uid uuid)` (in this order: read the email from `auth.users` into a variable BEFORE switching role — after `set role authenticated` with no claims set the `profiles` policy returns nothing and `login` is invoker; raise `test_failed` when the uid does not exist; then `execute 'set local role authenticated'`; then `set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', uid, 'role', 'authenticated', 'email', <that email>)::text, true)`), `app_test.login_anon()`, `app_test.login_service()` (`set local role service_role`, claims `{role: service_role}`), `app_test.logout()` (`reset role`, clear the claims), `app_test.assert_count(label text, sql text, expected bigint)` (`execute format('select count(*) from (%s) q', sql)`), `app_test.assert_true(label text, cond boolean)`, `app_test.assert_eq(label text, actual text, expected text)`, `app_test.assert_raises(label text, sql text, sqlstate text, message_key text default null)` (`begin … exception when others`; compares `sqlstate` and, when given, `sqlerrm`; fails when nothing is raised), `app_test.assert_denied(label text, sql text)` = `assert_raises(label, sql, '42501')`. Every failure raises `test_failed` with the label in `detail`; every pass emits `raise notice 'ok: <label>'`.
8. **`scripts/db/test.sh`** (extend the 1.2 stub): `cd "$REPO_ROOT"` first (test 08 uses a relative `\i`); apply `supabase/tests/helpers.sql` with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f`; run each `supabase/tests/rls/*.sql` in name order with `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q -f "$f" > "$log" 2>&1` (the `ok:` notices and error text go to stderr — without `2>&1` the failure excerpt is empty; `$log` lives under the session's scratchpad directory or `.local-pg/`, never `/tmp`), print `PASS <file>` / `FAIL <file>` (+ last 20 log lines on failure); optional `--only <name>`; summary `N passed, M failed`; exit 1 on any failure; keep the empty-directory branch. Every test file is plain SQL: it starts with `begin;` and ends with `rollback;` so nothing persists (test.sh supplies `-v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`; never put a psql meta-command such as `\set` in a test — the files must paste unchanged into the hosted SQL editor, DESIGN §12). The two documented exceptions (`\i` in 08, the fixture `\set` in 05 from step 1.4c) say so in their first comment line: `-- psql-only: <what> — skip/replace this line in the hosted SQL editor`.
9. **`supabase/tests/rls/01_tenancy.sql`**: build orgs A and B, fellowship F containing both, users `a_member` (A, no perms), `a_manager` (A, all 12), `b_member`, `super` (insert `super_admins`), one household + person + published sermon/announcement/bulletin/document + an `approved` calendar event + audience group in each org — all inserted under the identity rule of item 7 (logged out, or as the per-run super admin); assert the event is still `approved` and the person still `member` after insert (proves the convention). Assertions: (1) as `a_member`, for EVERY public table with an `org_id` column (plpgsql `do` loop over `pg_tables` joined to `pg_attribute`/`information_schema.columns` — iterate `pg_tables`, not `information_schema.tables`, so the three `directory_*` views are excluded; dynamic `select count(*) from public.%I where org_id = <B>`) the count is 0, and every other public table is selectable — a recursive policy would raise 42P17 here ("no 42P17 on any table"), so collect any SQLSTATE into a failure list; (2) `a_member` sees exactly 1 row in `organizations` when B does not share with the fellowship and 2 rows after `set_setting(B, 'directory_share_in_congregation','true')` + `directory_share_with_fellowship = true` (`ca_orgs_select_fellowship`); (3) `super` sees both orgs and every table's rows; (4) `login_anon()` then `select count(*) from public.organizations` → 42501 (`assert_denied`), likewise `public.sermons`, and `select public.my_context()` → 42501; (5) `login_service()` reads both orgs (BYPASSRLS); (6) `a_manager` sees A's `notifications`, `audit_log`, `billing_customers` but none of B's. 10. **`supabase/tests/rls/08_rerunnable.sql`**: inside the transaction snapshot into a temp table the counts of tables/views/policies (per table)/triggers/functions (per schema `app`,`public`)/indexes/enum types/`storage.buckets` rows/`storage.objects` policies; then `\i supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` (the migration has no `begin`/`commit`, so it re-applies inside the test transaction); snapshot again and assert identical counts and identical policy-name sets. Then assert: every function in `app` and `public` is `prosecdef` with `search_path=` in `proconfig`; every trigger function (`pg_trigger.tgfoid`) is `prosecdef`; every `pg_class` row in schema `public` with `relkind in ('r','p')` has `relrowsecurity` true and `relforcerowsecurity` false (views have neither); every policy in `public`/`storage` starts with `ca_`; `storage.objects` has exactly `ca_storage_select` and `ca_storage_insert`. First comment line: `-- psql-only: the \i line re-applies the migration; delete it in the hosted SQL editor (the count/prosecdef assertions still run)`.
11. **`supabase/tests/rls/09_grants.sql`**: (1) for every function in `public`, `has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'execute')` is false; (2) for every `public.srv_%` function, `has_function_privilege('authenticated', …)` is false and `has_function_privilege('service_role', …)` is true; (3) the set of `public` functions executable by `authenticated` equals exactly the 17 client RPC names listed in item 3 (compare sorted arrays; a new RPC must be added to both the grant and this list on purpose); (4) `anon` has zero rows in `information_schema.role_table_grants` for schema `public` and no `usage` on schema `private`; (5) `authenticated` has no `insert/update/delete` on any table of the RPC-only list in item 1 and no privilege at all on schema `private` tables; (6) `has_column_privilege('authenticated', 'public.persons', 'birthdate', 'select')` false, `… 'first_name' …` true, `households.anniversary` false, `households.hide_from_fellowship` false; (7) after `login(<member>)`: `select birthdate from public.persons` → 42501, `select * from public.persons` → 42501 (column-level), `select id, first_name from public.persons` succeeds; (8) `authenticated` can execute every helper the views and policies call (`app.household_view_level`, `app.is_adult`, `app.member_org_ids`, `app.fellowship_visible_org_ids`, `app.user_in_group`, `app.can_read_object`, `app.can_write_object`) and cannot execute `app.require_writable`, `app.rate_limit_hit`, `app.person_in_kind`, any trigger function; (9) `app_test` functions are executable by all three roles; (10) `has_table_privilege('authenticated', 'storage.objects', 'insert')` and `has_table_privilege('service_role', 'storage.objects', 'delete')` are true (shim parity with Supabase; 1.4c's storage tests depend on it). 12. **Docs**: `docs/ENV.md` "Local database" — one line on `pnpm db:test` and `bash scripts/db/test.sh --only 09_grants`. CI needs no change (the DB job already runs the standing sequence).

## Constraints
- Migration rules (CLAUDE.md, PLAN §4, DESIGN §12): every policy `drop … if exists` then `create`; names start with `ca_`; no `force row level security`; functions untouched unless a signature must change (then drop dependents first in the same file); pgcrypto/citext schema-qualified; the file must apply twice in a row; never `supabase db push` / `db reset`; never `supabase start`.
- Policies are split per operation and use the InitPlan form (`perm_org_ids`, never per-row `app.has_perm`); never derive permissions from `auth.jwt()` claims.
- No policies for `service_role`; no grants to `anon`; no `security_invoker` on views; do not add tables, columns or RPCs (missing pieces → HANDOFF "Deviations from plan", fix in place only when a policy cannot be written otherwise).
- The `sermon-media` limit lives in exactly one place (the `c_sermon_media_limit` constant); do not repeat `2147483648` anywhere except in that comment.
- Tests: plain SQL that pastes unchanged into the hosted SQL editor (no psql meta-commands except the documented `\i` in 08), one rolled-back transaction per file, no `\connect`, no uuids in the seed range `00000000-0000-4000-8000-…` (step 1.5), no real email addresses (`<slug>@example.test`); every shell path quoted; nothing under `/tmp`.
- Do not write `02`–`07` here (steps 1.4b/1.4c), the seed, `gen-types.sh`, `docs/RLS.md` or `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` (step 1.5). No npm dependencies. `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` must stay green.

## Verify
- A plain `bash scripts/db/local-up.sh` on the EXISTING local database (no drop) followed by `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select rolbypassrls from pg_roles where rolname = 'service_role'"` → `t`, and `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select has_table_privilege('authenticated','storage.objects','insert')"` → `t` (proves the shim is re-applied every run).
- `bash scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && bash scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh` → both exit 0.
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname = 'public' and not rowsecurity"` → `0`; `select count(*) from pg_policies where schemaname in ('public','storage') and policyname not like 'ca\_%'` → `0`; `select count(*) from pg_policies where schemaname = 'storage'` → `2`; `… where schemaname = 'public'` ≥ 90; `select count(*) from storage.buckets` → `5`; `select file_size_limit from storage.buckets where id = 'sermon-media'` → `52428800`.
- `psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "select count(*) from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and has_function_privilege('authenticated', p.oid, 'execute')"` → `17`; the same for `service_role` restricted to `proname like 'srv\_%'` → `7`; for `anon` → `0`.
- `bash scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh` → `OK supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql`. (Checkpoint commit here — see Build.)
- `grep -L '^begin;' supabase/tests/rls/*.sql` → empty; `grep -l '\\set' supabase/tests/rls/*.sql` → empty (no psql meta-commands besides 08's `\i`).
- `bash scripts/db/test.sh` → `PASS supabase/tests/rls/01_tenancy.sql`, `PASS …/08_rerunnable.sql`, `PASS …/09_grants.sql`, `3 passed, 0 failed`, exit 0; `bash scripts/db/test.sh --only 09_grants` runs one file.
- Negative check: break one assertion in `01_tenancy`, see `FAIL` + exit 1, restore it.
- The standing sequence `scripts/db/local-up.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/apply-migrations.sh && scripts/db/check-rerunnable.sh && scripts/db/test.sh` → exit 0.
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green; `pnpm format:check` → clean.
- After the push, the CI DB job passes (fresh `postgres:16` service via `PG_SUPER_URL`).

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: State sub-bullet "9999_init.sql sections 8–11 + SQL test harness (step 1.4a)"; record the policy count, the granted RPC lists, the `c_sermon_media_limit` constant (50 MiB, Free) and that raising it on Pro is a new `supabase/migrations/9995_storage_limit.sql` (bucket upsert for `sermon-media` only), never an edit of 9999; record the fixture identity rule (item 7) and the `app_test` signatures; under "Deviations from plan" list every ambiguous DESIGN §6 row and your choice (events insert `∨ announcements.create`, surveys three-key select), the explicit table-grant block, any grant signature that differed from DESIGN, the shim tweaks (bypassrls, storage RLS, storage table grants) and the `local-up.sh` change. Founder to-do: if the step 2.4 paste fails on the `storage.objects` policies, see step 1.8 if the orchestrator adopted it; otherwise re-run only section (10) after checking `select tableowner from pg_tables where schemaname = 'storage'` in the hosted project.
- Tick step 1.4a in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(db): RLS policy catalogue, grants, storage buckets and SQL test harness`; push `main` (`git push origin main`).
- If anything in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.

Tag the block as a whole with acceptance: "12 permissions positive/negative".
   - `my_context()`: `manager` → `is_super_admin = false`, one org with all 12 `permissions` (compare as sorted arrays), `membership_status = 'active'`; `nobody` → `person_id` and `household_id` present (linked person); `loner` → `orgs = '[]'`; a super admin (`make_super`) → `is_super_admin = true`. Assert the exact keys 1.3b documented — step 1.7's wrappers and 2.1's guards deserialise this shape.

2. **`03_directory_visibility.sql`** — fellowship F = {A, B, C}; org D outside F. Settings: A and B share in congregation and with fellowship; C shares in congregation only; D shares with fellowship (but is not in F). Users: `a_member` (A, no perms, linked to an adult in A), `b_member` (B, no perms, linked to an adult of H4 — so the "own household" assertions below have a household to point at), `b_admin` (B, `users.create` only — a directory admin by decision 4), `b_settings` (B, `org.settings` only — also a directory admin), `b_head` (B, no perms, linked to the head of household H1), `b_spouse` (linked to H1's spouse), `super` (`make_super`). Households in B, each with adults and where noted children: H1 (normal: head, spouse, child aged 8 with birthdate, `show_children_in_fellowship = false`), H2 (`hide_from_fellowship = true`), H3 (`hide_from_congregation = true`), H4 (`show_children_in_fellowship = true`, one child aged 10, plus the adult linked to `b_member`), H5 (`created_via = 'admin'` — must default to `hide_from_fellowship = true`), H6 (adult with `directory_listed = false`, adult `congregation_status = 'inactive'`, adult with `deceased_on` set), H7 (person `household_role = 'other'` with no birthdate; adult with `birthdate_visibility = 'full'`; adult with `'hidden'`). One household each in A, C and D. Assertions (use `directory_persons` / `directory_households` unless stated):

Then `set_setting(B, 'fellowship_directory_adults_only', 'false')` → `a_member` now also sees H1's child; restore to `true` → gone again.
   - `org_directory_info`: `a_member` sees exactly A and B (name, slug, logo_path) — not C (no fellowship sharing) nor D (not in F); `b_member` sees A and B; a D member sees only D.
   - `b_member` (congregation level) sees H1, H2, H4, H5 (hidden-from-fellowship does not hide from the congregation), H7; not H3 (`hide_from_congregation`), not the unlisted/inactive/deceased persons; `birthday_display` is `YYYY-MM-DD` for `full`, `MM-DD` for `month_day`, null for `hidden`; `birthdate`, `member_since`, `youth_override` are null. After `set_setting(B, 'directory_share_with_fellowship', 'false')` then `set_setting(B, 'directory_share_in_congregation', 'false')` (that order satisfies the check) `b_member` sees only H4 (own household, `view_level = 'household'`) and `a_member` sees nothing from B; restore both.
   - `b_head` sees every person of H1 including the child, with `birthdate`, `view_level = 'household'`; `b_admin` and `b_settings` see every household and person of B including H3 and H6's hidden persons (`view_level = 'admin'`), with `member_since` and `youth_override`; `super` sees everything in every org.
   - Column-level (acceptance: "`select birthdate from persons` → 42501"): after `login(b_member)`, `select birthdate from public.persons` → 42501, `select anniversary from public.households` → 42501, `select * from public.persons` → 42501; `select count(*) from public.persons` (base table, allowed columns only) equals the count from `directory_persons` for that viewer (PLAN §5: base-table policy = view rule).

H5 (`created_via = 'admin'`) has `hide_from_fellowship = true` without anyone touching it (acceptance: "admin-created household hidden from fellowship by default") and an adult of H5 linked to a user can flip it to false.
   - Household RPCs: `save_household` by `b_head` (update H1's address) → ok and visible; by `b_member` on H1 → `not_household_editor`; `b_admin` creating a household via `save_household` (no `id`) → row with `created_via = 'admin'` and `hide_from_fellowship = true`; `delete_person` by `b_head` on H1's child → gone; on an H2 person → `not_household_editor` (or 42501 — assert what 1.3b raises); on H1's only `head` → assert the 1.3b behaviour (refused with its key, or allowed) and note it in HANDOFF for 5.1.

   - Org status: `update organizations set status = 'suspended' where id = B` (as service) → `a_member` sees no B households, no B row in `organizations` and no B row in `org_directory_info`; back to `active` → visible again.
3. **`04_sermons_share_links.sql`** — org S with `linker` (`sermons.link`), `uploader` (`sermons.upload`), `member` (none); one published upload sermon `sermon_up` (`storage_path = S/sermons/<id>/a.mp3`), one published youtube sermon `sermon_yt`, one draft. Correct password on an unlocked token → `ok`, `view_count = 1`, `allow_download = false`, and the payload fields as 1.3b documented them in HANDOFF/`9999_init.sql` (at minimum the sermon's media kind and the org slug under whatever keys 1.3b chose — do not rename them); `set_setting(S, 'sermon_share_allow_download', 'true')` → `allow_download = true` for the upload link and `false` for a link on `sermon_yt` (founder decision 5: uploaded media only); a link created with `max_views = 1` → second `ok`… → `max_views`; a link with `expires_at = now() - interval '1 minute'` → `expired`; `revoke_share_link` by `linker` → `revoked` (and `member` → `permission_denied`); `set_setting(S, 'sermons_shareable', 'false')` → `sharing_disabled` for a valid link (acceptance: "share link fails after org disables sharing"); re-enable and `update sermons set publish_at = null` → `unpublished`; `set_setting(S, 'sermon_share_requires_password', 'false')`, create a passwordless link, then set it back to true → `needs_password_reset`; unknown hash → `invalid`; `login(member)` then `srv_resolve_share_link(...)` → 42501; `login_anon()` → 42501. Assert an `audit_log` row exists for the share-link insert and for the revoke.

Shape: `{ "settings": { "timezone": "America/New_York", "youth_min_age": 13, "youth_max_age": 25, "adult_min_age": 18, "youth_excludes_married": true, "adult_groups_include_youth": true }, "persons": [ { "key": "…", "first_name": "…", "sex": "male"|"female"|null, "age_years": <int|null>, "birthday_offset_days": <int, default 0>, "marital_status": "…", "household_role": "…", "congregation_status": "…", "deceased": false, "youth_override": null|true|false, "in_custom_group": false, "expected": { "everyone": bool, "members": bool, "attendees": bool, "youth": bool, "men": bool, "women": bool, "custom": bool } } ] }`. Ages are relative so the test never rots: birthdate = (today in the org timezone) − `age_years` years − `birthday_offset_days` days; `birthday_offset_days = -1` with `age_years = 13` means "turns 13 tomorrow" (still 12). Cover at least: adult male member; adult female attendee; youth 13 male (in youth and, with `adult_groups_include_youth`, in men); youth 25 female; 26-year-old (not youth); married 20-year-old with `youth_excludes_married` (not youth, in women); `youth_override = true` on a 40-year-old; `youth_override = false` on a 16-year-old; child 8 with birthdate (nowhere but everyone/attendees); child role with no birthdate; role `other` with no birthdate (everyone; men/women per DESIGN §4.3 "counted in men/women"); deceased member (nowhere); inactive youth (nowhere); the turns-13-tomorrow edge; the turns-18-today edge; a custom-group member. Add a top-level comment field `"_note": "ages relative to today in settings.timezone; consumers (05_audiences.sql, packages/domain audiences.test.ts) must pass an explicit today in the org timezone"` so 1.6's Vitest never uses UTC `new Date()`.
2. **`05_audiences.sql`** — `make_org`, apply `settings` via `set_setting`. Loading the fixture is the ONE place a psql meta-command is allowed: line 1 is the comment `-- psql-only: the \set line below reads the fixture from disk; in the hosted SQL editor replace it with the file's JSON pasted as a dollar-quoted literal`, line 2 is `\set fixture `cat packages/domain/fixtures/persons.json`` and the only other place the variable appears is one statement right after `begin;`: `select set_config('app_test.fixture', :'fixture', true);` — everywhere else read `current_setting('app_test.fixture')::jsonb`, so a hosted run changes exactly one line. Then for each element of `jsonb_array_elements(... -> 'persons')` insert one household + person via the builders (birthdate computed as `(now() at time zone <settings.timezone>)::date - (age_years * interval '1 year') - (birthday_offset_days * interval '1 day')`), and for each person and each of the six kinds assert `app.person_in_kind(id, kind) = expected` (raise with the person key and kind on mismatch); create one custom `audience_groups` row + `audience_group_members` for the flagged persons and assert `app.person_in_group` on it. Timezone edge (DESIGN §4.3 "timezone edge", PLAN §4 "age computed in the org timezone"): `set_setting(org, 'timezone', 'Pacific/Kiritimati')` (UTC+14) and insert a person whose birthdate = `(now() at time zone 'Pacific/Kiritimati')::date - interval '18 years'` → `app.is_adult(...)` true and `person_in_kind(id, 'men')` true; then `set_setting(org, 'timezone', 'Pacific/Pago_Pago')` (UTC−11; its calendar date is always one day behind Kiritimati) → the same person is 17 → `is_adult` false — this fails if `person_age` used `current_date`. Then `srv_audience_user_ids` (acceptance: "disabled membership absent from `srv_audience_user_ids`"): link users to three persons, `make_member` two `active` and one with `status => 'disabled'`; `login_service()` → the result contains the two active user ids and not the disabled one, persons without `user_id` are absent, `group_id = null` means everyone; `login(<active user>)` → `srv_audience_user_ids` → 42501. `app.user_in_group(null)` is true for every authenticated caller (null group = everyone, DESIGN §4.3), with or without a linked person; for any non-null group a member without a linked person gets false. Finally `set_setting(org, 'adult_groups_include_youth', 'false')` → the 13-year-old leaves `men`; `youth_excludes_married = false` → the married 20-year-old joins `youth`.
3. **`06_events_surveys.sql`** — org E with `creator` (`announcements.create`), `editor` (`announcements.edit`), `deleter` (`announcements.delete`), `member` (no perms, linked to an adult male person, `congregation_status = 'member'`, in `everyone`), `member_f` (no perms, linked to an adult female member), `member2` (no perms, NO linked person), `outsider` (member of another org X); `bull` (`bulletins.upload`).
   - Events (acceptance: "member event forced to pending/push=false"): `member` inserts into `events` on the `all` calendar with `status = 'approved', push = true, submitted_by = auth.uid()` → row stored as `pending`, `push = false`; `creator` inserts approved → stays `approved` and one `notifications` row (`kind = 'event'`, `ref_id`) appears; `member` sees own pending event and the approved one, `member2` sees only the approved one; `member` updates own pending title → 1 row; `member` updating own `status = 'approved'` → 42501 (with check); `editor` sets `status = 'approved'` → ok and a notification is enqueued; `set_setting(E, 'members_can_submit_events', 'false')` → `member` insert → 42501 while `creator` still can (the 1.4a policy reading); restore; `set_setting(E, 'events_require_approval', 'false')` → a `member` insert is stored as `approved` with `push = false` (or whatever 1.3a's `force_event_pending` implements — assert it and record the behaviour in HANDOFF so 5.3's approval queue matches); restore to true; a calendar with `submit_audience_group_id` = the `men` group → `member_f`'s insert → 42501, `member`'s → ok; a calendar with `view_audience_group_id` = `men` → invisible to `member_f` (0 rows in `calendars`) and so are its events, visible to `member`; `deleter` deletes → gone, `member` deleting another's event → 0 rows; deleting an event with a queued notification → that notification `cancelled`; `outsider` sees 0 events and 0 calendars of E; `audience_group_members` select → 0 rows for `member`, ≥ 1 for `creator`; `fellowships`: put E in a fellowship F → `member` sees F, `outsider` 0 rows.
   - Notifications lifecycle (DESIGN §4.4/§8; founder decision 6): `creator` inserts an announcement with `publish_at = now() + interval '1 day'` → no `notifications` row; `login_service()`, `update announcements set publish_at = now() - interval '1 minute'`, `select public.srv_enqueue_due_notifications()` → exactly one `queued` row with `kind = 'announcement'` and that `ref_id`; a second `srv_enqueue_due_notifications()` adds nothing (idempotent). `bull` inserts a bulletin (`publish_at = now()`) → one `kind = 'bulletin'` row; `set_setting(E, 'push_on_bulletin', 'false')` → another bulletin → no new row; restore. `srv_claim_notifications(10)` → returns the queued rows, each now `status = 'claimed'`, `attempts = 1`, `claimed_at` set; a second call returns 0 rows; `login(creator)` → `srv_claim_notifications(10)` → 42501; `creator` sees E's `notifications` rows, `member` 0 rows.
   - Surveys: `creator` inserts a `draft` survey (`audience_group_id = everyone`, `per_person`) with two questions; `member` sees 0 surveys while draft; `creator` sets `status = 'open'` → `member` sees it and its questions; `editor` changing `response_mode` after open → `survey_shape_frozen` (P0001), inserting a question → `survey_shape_frozen`; `member` `submit_survey_response(survey, '{"<q1>": "a", "<q2>": 3}')` → uuid, `survey_responses` has `person_id = member's person`, `scope_key = 'p:<person>'`, `submitted_by_user_id`; unknown question key → `invalid_payload`; `outsider` → `survey_not_in_audience` (or 42501 — assert what is raised, note it); with `allow_edit = false` a second submit → `survey_already_responded` or `survey_edit_not_allowed` — assert the key 1.3b's catalogue assigns to this case and record it in HANDOFF for 1.6's `errors.ts`; with `allow_edit = true` a second submit updates in place (still 1 response row, answers replaced); `member2` without a linked person → `no_person_linked`; a `per_household` survey: head submits, spouse of the same household submits → `survey_already_responded` (acceptance: "per-household survey double-response rejected"); `closes_at` in the past → `survey_not_open`; `status = 'closed'` → `survey_not_open`; responses visible to their owner and to `creator`, not to `member2`; a survey with `audience_group_id = men` is invisible to `member_f`; opening a survey with `push = true` enqueues a `notifications` row (`kind = 'survey'`).
4. **`07_storage_billing_audit.sql`** — (a) Storage helpers called directly as roles: org O with `uploader` (`sermons.upload`), `bull` (`bulletins.upload`), `doc` (`documents.upload`), `settings` (`org.settings`), `member` (linked adult female), `head` (household adult of H), `deleter` (`sermons.delete`), `super`. Draft sermon with `storage_path = O/sermons/<id>/x.mp3`: `app.can_write_object('sermon-media', <that path>)` true for `uploader`, false for `member`, false for `uploader` on `O/sermons/<id>/other.mp3` (must equal exactly), false for a path with a malformed uuid, false for a path under another org; `can_read_object` on the draft: `uploader` true, `member` false; after `publish_at = now()`: `member` true, `login_anon()` → 42501 on the function call (no grant). `bulletins`, `documents` (published + `audience_group_id` = `men` → `member` (female) reads false), `directory-photos` (`O/households/<H>/p.jpg`: `head` write true when `households.photo_path` equals it, `member` write false, read true for a congregation member, false when the household is hidden from the congregation; `O/persons/<child>/p.jpg` write by `head` true), `org-assets` (`O/logo/<uuid>.png`: write requires `org.settings` and `organization_settings.logo_path` = path; read true for a member and for a fellowship-visible viewer). (b) Storage policies through the table (the shim grants the table privileges; the policies filter): `login(uploader)` → `insert into storage.objects (bucket_id, name) values ('sermon-media', <exact path>)` → ok; a different name → 42501; `update storage.objects set name = …` and `delete from storage.objects` as `uploader` → 0 rows affected, row still there (no policies); `login_service()` deletes it. Deleting the sermon row as `deleter` → one `storage_deletions` row (`bucket_id = 'sermon-media'`, `object_name = path`, `is_prefix = false`); readable by `super` only (`assert_count` 0 for `settings`, 1 for `super`). (c) Billing (founder decision 7): `make_org(P)` starts `trial`; `login_service()` insert `billing_customers` + `billing_subscriptions (status = 'active')` with `billing_mode = 'manual'` → `organizations.status` unchanged; set `billing_mode = 'stripe'` and update the subscription to `active` → `status = 'active'`; `past_due` → `past_due`, and a `sermons.upload` holder can STILL insert a sermon and call `create_share_link` (past_due = banner only); `canceled` → `suspended`; now (acceptance: "suspended org rejects mutating RPCs") every mutating client RPC raises `organization_suspended` (42501): `set_membership_permissions`, `set_membership_status`, `remove_membership`, `create_invitation`, `revoke_invitation`, `accept_invitation(<token of a pending invitation created in P before the suspension>)`, `save_household`, `save_person`, `delete_person`, `set_household_privacy`, `save_leader_notes`, `set_congregation_status`, `create_share_link`, `revoke_share_link`, `submit_survey_response` (plausible arguments; if 1.3b validates arguments before `require_writable`, assert what it raises and note it); `request_account_deletion()` is user-scoped, not org-scoped — it must still succeed for a member of the suspended org (assert a row in `account_deletion_requests`, Play Store requirement); direct `insert into sermons` → 42501, `update organization_settings` → 0 rows; reads still work (`my_context()` returns the org with `status = 'suspended'`, `select` on sermons returns rows); `billing_customers`/`billing_subscriptions` readable by `settings` and `super`, 0 rows for `member`; `stripe_events` 0 rows for everyone but `super`. (d) Audit: permission change via `set_membership_permissions` → `audit_log` rows for `org_membership_permissions` with `actor_user_id` = caller; `set_household_privacy` → an `audit_log` row whose `new_data` contains `hide_from_fellowship` and NOT `first_name`/`notes`; `save_leader_notes` → no `audit_log` row mentioning the notes text (`assert_count` of rows where `new_data::text like '%<notes text>%'` = 0); `audit_log` readable by `settings` and `super`, 0 rows for `member`; `login(member)` `insert into audit_log` → 42501; `update organization_settings set timezone = 'Mars/Olympus'` → `invalid_timezone` (22023). (e) Server RPCs (DESIGN §4.4 semantics; all as `login_service()`, and each → 42501 as `login(member)`): `srv_attach_user(<new uid>, O, null, 'New Person', '{sermons.upload}')` → active membership, a one-person household (`created_via = 'admin'`, hence `hide_from_fellowship = true`), person linked with `household_role = 'head'`, 1 permission row; calling it again for the same user → idempotent or the 1.3b key (assert what is implemented, note it for 3.2's `createUserDirect`); with a `person_id` of an existing unlinked adult → that person is linked, no new household. `srv_housekeeping()`: an org with `trial_ends_at = now() - interval '1 day'`, `billing_mode = 'manual'` → `status = 'past_due'`; an invitation past `expires_at` → `accept_invitation` → `invitation_invalid`; an upload-kind draft sermon with `created_at = now() - interval '8 days'` and no `storage.objects` row → deleted, while a fresh draft and a draft whose object exists survive; an org set to `cancelled` with the status timestamp 31 days ago (use whatever column 1.3b reads) → the org row is gone and `storage_deletions` has one `is_prefix = true` row per bucket for the `<org_id>/` prefix; `private.rate_limits` rows older than the window are pruned. `request_account_deletion()` as `member` → a row in `account_deletion_requests`; make that member the only `users.edit_permissions` holder of O first; `srv_process_account_deletions()` → the `auth.users` row is gone, `processed_at` set, memberships gone, and an `audit_log` row with `action = 'org_without_manager'` for O exists (the last-manager guard is skipped under `app.cascade = 'on'`).
5. **Wire-up**: `scripts/db/test.sh` needs no change. Keep the fixture Prettier-formatted. Record every migration fix in a `-- fix (step 1.4c): …` comment next to the change.

## Constraints
- Fix migration bugs in place, keeping every construct re-runnable (`check-rerunnable.sh` after each edit) and the section order. Never `supabase db push`/`db reset`.
- Tests are deterministic (relative ages; the timezone edge uses two zones whose calendar dates never coincide; no wall-clock dependence otherwise), plain SQL except the single documented `\set` line in 05, use no real email addresses or seed-range uuids (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-…`), depend on no other file's data, and roll back.
- Follow the fixture identity rule from `helpers.sql`; never `alter table … disable trigger` and never weaken a guard to make a fixture pass.
- Do not change the fixture shape once written without updating this step's notes in HANDOFF — step 1.6's Vitest suite depends on it. No npm dependencies; do not touch `packages/domain/src` (step 1.6). `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` must stay green (the JSON fixture is data, not source).

## Verify

- `bash scripts/db/test.sh` → `PASS` for all nine files, `9 passed, 0 failed`, exit 0. Run each new file alone with `--only` at least once.
- Acceptance tags: `grep -h '^-- acceptance:' supabase/tests/rls/*.sql | sort -u | wc -l` → `18` (all PLAN §12 DB sentences: the 14 from 1.4a/1.4b plus "disabled membership absent from `srv_audience_user_ids`", "per-household survey double-response rejected", "member event forced to pending/push=false", "suspended org rejects mutating RPCs").
- `head -1 supabase/tests/rls/05_audiences.sql` starts with `-- psql-only:`; `grep -c "current_setting('app_test.fixture')" supabase/tests/rls/05_audiences.sql` ≥ 2 and `grep -c ":'fixture'" …` = 1 (single substitution point).
- `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('packages/domain/fixtures/persons.json')); assert len(d['persons']) >= 16"` → ok; `pnpm format:check` clean.
- Negative check: flip one `expected` value in the fixture, see `05_audiences` fail naming the person key, restore it.
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green. CI DB job passes on the push.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: tick "`supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` + local shim + RLS tests" in State; in "Founder's feature checklist" set the `Schema` column of every row except `iOS build` to `done (9999_init.sql, tested 01–09)` (leave Web UI / Mobile UI unchanged); record every migration fix made here under "Deviations from plan" (with the test that found it), the fixture shape (`age_years` relative ages, `expected` map, the `today`-in-org-timezone rule) for step 1.6, the `events_require_approval = false` behaviour for 5.3, the `srv_attach_user` repeat-call behaviour for 3.2, and any RPC error key you had to assert differently from the 1.3b catalogue (`survey_already_responded` vs `survey_edit_not_allowed`, outsider on `submit_survey_response`).
- Tick step 1.4c in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `test(db): behavioural RLS tests for audiences, events, surveys, notifications, storage, billing, audit and server RPCs`; push `main`.
- If anything in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.

reads: docs/DESIGN.md §2 (supabase/ and scripts/db entries), §5 (mapping, bootstrap order), §6 (directory rule), §11 Founder action items, §12 (type generation), §13 risks 1–4, 7, 11, 13–15
supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql (all sections — the docs describe the real file), supabase/tests/rls/*.sql, packages/domain/fixtures/persons.json

steps.notes: One session: one large SQL seed, two small scripts, three documents, a generated file. Depends on 1.4c (the second split of the behavioural tests; `9 passed` is reached there). Deviations from the skeleton bullet: the generated `database.types.ts` is produced and committed here (the skeleton lists it under 1.7 as well) so the CI drift check activates and 1.7 starts from a real file — G4 (1.7) should regenerate rather than create it. Typegen: the Supabase CLI's `gen types --db-url` runs postgres-meta in Docker, which the agents' machines lack, so `gen-types.sh` runs `@supabase/postgres-meta` directly under Node (exact-pinned root devDependency, `/generators/typescript` endpoint) — unconditionally, also in CI, for byte-identical output; this is the one dependency the step adds. `scripts/db/seed.sh` (local-only guard, `--i-know-this-is-not-production`) and the root `db:seed` script are additions (the docs only name the seed file) — flagged in open_issues. The seed inserts the `super_admins` row before setting the claims to the seed super admin and asserts `app.is_super_admin()`, so every trigger guard passes; if a guard ignores super admins the seed runs that part under the org admin's claims. The share link and invitation are created through `create_share_link` / `create_invitation` (not by hand) so the token/hash convention stays single-sourced; the printed tokens and password are local conveniences. Raising the `sermon-media` limit on Pro is documented everywhere (runbook, MIGRATIONS.md worked example, HANDOFF) as a new `9995_storage_limit.sql`, never as an edit of the frozen 9999. The hosted test run instructions name the two psql-only edits (05 fixture line, 08 `\i`) and require `drop schema app_test cascade` afterwards. `docs/PLAN.md`/`docs/DESIGN.md` are deliberately not edited for the Free/Pro wording (orchestrator decision 4 calls it historical); HANDOFF and the runbook carry the truth, and Vercel Pro / the founder-answers table are left alone. Role-header labels (Sermon manager / Announcement manager / Organization manager) are chosen here and recorded in HANDOFF Decisions for 1.6 and 3.2.

open_issues: Step 1.4 is now split three ways (orchestrator decision 13 + the critics' sizing review): 1.4a (migration sections 8–11 + helpers.sql + test.sh + tests 01/08/09, with a mandatory checkpoint commit after sections 8–11), 1.4b (tests 02–04) and 1.4c (fixture + tests 05–07 + server RPC / notification coverage). The orchestrator must propagate: 1.5 depends on 1.4c (done in this file); any other group that says 'RLS tests from 1.4' or '1.4b' for the fixture / `9 passed` means 1.4c; '1.4 depends on 1.3' is 1.3b (G2 split).

Prompt length: 1.4a (~4450 words) and 1.5 (~4100 words) exceed orchestrator decision 9's 1200–3000 range after the critics' additions (the validator only warns). The reviser was told not to shorten; the assembler may trim boilerplate or accept the length for these two DB-heavy steps.

Policy names beyond the four DESIGN spells out (`ca_orgs_select_fellowship`, `ca_sermons_select_members`, `ca_sermons_insert_by_kind`, `ca_persons_select_visible`, `ca_profiles_select_org_admin`, `ca_storage_select`, `ca_storage_insert`) follow `ca_<table>_<op>_<who>` and are chosen by the 1.4a agent; docs/RLS.md (1.5) documents the real names from pg_policies, so no other group should hard-code them.

The `app_test` helper API (make_user/make_org/make_member(org, uid, perms, status default 'active')/make_fellowship/make_household/make_person/make_super/set_setting/sha256_token as definer; login/login_anon/login_service/logout/assert_count/assert_true/assert_eq/assert_raises/assert_denied as invoker) is defined in 1.4a, together with the fixture identity rule (builders run logged out; if 1.3a's guards do not trust a null `auth.uid()`, builders switch to a per-run super admin's claims for the call). G13 (5.6 join-code tests) and G14 (6.1 survey tests) should reuse it rather than define their own.

Deviations from DESIGN made explicit in 1.4a and to be recorded in HANDOFF: an explicit table-grant block (DESIGN §4.4 relies on Supabase default privileges; the shim has none — every `9998_*` table needs its own grant lines, documented in docs/MIGRATIONS.md by 1.5); the events insert policy adds `∨ announcements.create` to `members_can_submit_events` (DESIGN §6 lists only the setting); the surveys select uses the three-key `announcements.create/edit/delete` form (DESIGN §6 says `announcements.create`).

1.4c creates `packages/domain/fixtures/persons.json` (the skeleton assigns it to 1.6). Shape: `{_note, settings: {timezone, youth_min_age, youth_max_age, adult_min_age, youth_excludes_married, adult_groups_include_youth}, persons: [{key, first_name, sex, age_years, birthday_offset_days, marital_status, household_role, congregation_status, deceased, youth_override, in_custom_group, expected: {everyone, members, attendees, youth, men, women, custom}}]}` with ages relative to 'today in the org timezone'. G4 (1.6 `audiences.ts` + Vitest) must consume this file, compute birthdates the same way with an explicit `today` in the org timezone (never UTC `new Date()`), and may add fields but not rename them.

Hosted verbatim run (DESIGN §12): all test files are plain SQL except two documented psql-only lines — `05_audiences.sql` reads the fixture with a `\set` (single substitution point; replace with a dollar-quoted JSON literal or skip the file) and `08_rerunnable.sql` re-applies the migration with `\i` (delete the line). Both say so in their first comment line and 1.5's runbook explains the edits plus `drop schema app_test cascade` afterwards. If the orchestrator wants a fully verbatim hosted run, 08 could drop the re-apply and 05 could embed the JSON — at the cost of duplicating the fixture.

1.5 generates and commits `packages/db/src/database.types.ts` (the skeleton lists the generated file under 1.7 too). Typegen does NOT use `supabase gen types --db-url` (the CLI runs postgres-meta in Docker, unavailable on the agents' machines); `scripts/db/gen-types.sh` runs `@supabase/postgres-meta` directly under Node (exact-pinned root devDependency — the one dependency 1.5 adds — `/generators/typescript?included_schemas=public&detect_one_to_one_relationships=true`), unconditionally, also in CI, for byte-identical output. G4 (1.7) should regenerate with `pnpm db:types` and build `client.ts`/`rpc.ts` on top, not create the file; G1's CI drift step already calls `gen-types.sh`. 1.5 also adds `src/database.types.ts` to the ESLint ignores of `packages/db`. Risk: the package's server entry path (`dist/server/server.js`) must be confirmed from its package.json by the agent.

Local-only shim tweaks in 1.4a: `alter role service_role bypassrls`, `alter table storage.objects enable row level security`, and `grant select, insert, update, delete on storage.objects, storage.buckets to authenticated, service_role` in `supabase/tests/00_shim.sql`; `scripts/db/local-up.sh` (G2, 1.2) is changed to re-apply the idempotent shim on every run instead of skipping it when `auth.uid()` exists, so existing databases pick the tweaks up without a drop. G2's 1.2 done_when bullet 'is skipped when auth.uid() already exists' becomes stale after 1.4a.

Creating policies on `storage.objects` as `postgres` in the hosted SQL editor is standard Supabase practice but unproven here until step 2.4; G2's proposed step 1.8 (throwaway-project dry run) is the mitigation and is endorsed by G3 (1.4a's HANDOFF note says 'see 1.8 if adopted; otherwise re-run section (10) after checking the storage table owner').

Raising the `sermon-media` limit on Pro: the constant `c_sermon_media_limit` in section (10) stays at 50 MiB; the sanctioned raise is a new `supabase/migrations/9998_storage_limit.sql` (bucket upsert for `sermon-media` only, 2 GiB) — the constant's comment, 1.5's runbook, docs/MIGRATIONS.md's worked example and HANDOFF all say so; 9999 is never edited after it is in the ledger. The name `9998_storage_limit.sql` is chosen here; whichever group ships the first real `9998_*` migration (5.6's `9998_join_codes.sql` per the skeleton) must renumber one of them (the storage-limit file may become `9997_*` or later — the docs say 'a new migration', the number is assigned when it is written).

Behaviours 1.4b/1.4c assert but 1.3b leaves open (outsider calling `submit_survey_response`: `survey_not_in_audience` vs 42501; `survey_already_responded` vs `survey_edit_not_allowed` when `allow_edit = false`; cross-org `set_membership_permissions`: `permission_denied` vs `membership_not_found`; invitation expiry key; `delete_person` on the only head; whether the `needs_password` probe counts toward the 10-failure lock; the resolve payload's sermon/org keys; `events_require_approval = false` semantics; `srv_attach_user` repeat call; whether `require_writable` fires before argument validation) are asserted as implemented and recorded in HANDOFF; G4 (1.6 errors.ts), G7 (3.2), G8 (3.4), G9 (3.6), G12 (5.1, 5.3) should read that record.

Names chosen in 1.5 because the docs leave them open: `scripts/db/seed.sh` (local-only guard, `--i-know-this-is-not-production`) and the root `db:seed` script; the three permission-grid role-header labels `Sermon manager` / `Announcement manager` / `Organization manager` (recorded in HANDOFF Decisions; G4's 1.6 `permissions.ts` and G7's 3.2 grid must reuse them); the `-- acceptance:` tag convention (18 PLAN §12 DB sentences) that docs/RLS.md lists. G10 (3.7) and any hosted-seed variant must reuse the seed script names.

Seed accounts use `<name>@example.test` addresses, fixed uuids in `00000000-0000-4000-8000-…`, the local password `seed-password-1` for the share link, printed invitation/share tokens, and syntactically valid example YouTube/Dropbox URLs; the seed is local-only and refuses non-local `DATABASE_URL`. Steps 2.x/3.x that want seeded data for Playwright (3.7) must note the seed cannot run against a hosted project (auth.users inserts) — G10 may want a hosted-seed variant through `auth.admin.createUser` + `srv_attach_user`.

Orchestrator decision 4 says PLAN/DESIGN 'Pro recommended' wording is historical; 1.5 fixes HANDOFF (Supabase item only — Vercel Pro and the founder-answers table row 10 stay), README, and the new docs only and does not edit docs/PLAN.md §12 / DESIGN §11 — the assembler may want a one-line note in those files.

Supabase Auth URL configuration cannot be completed at step 2.4 (the Vercel URL exists only after 2.5): 1.5's runbook and HANDOFF say 'localhost redirect now, Site URL + `<VERCEL_URL>/auth/callback` after 2.5'. G6 (2.4/2.5 checklists) should mirror that order.
